text: By default, printing an object shows an ugly memory address — dunder methods fix that beautifully.
The dunder-str method defines the friendly, readable version shown to end users.
So print of a point now shows those clean coordinates instead of gibberish.
[chuckle] dunder-repr is the developer-facing version, meant to be unambiguous and ideally reconstructable.
By convention, repr looks like the code you'd type to recreate the object — Point of three, four.
[sniff] print and str use dunder-str, while repr and the interactive prompt use dunder-repr.
If you only define one, define repr — Python falls back to it when str is missing.
[sigh] And notice — printing a list of objects uses repr for each element, not str.
[groan] Adding these two methods turns your objects from cryptic to crystal clear in every print and debug session.
